text: An old man is sweeping the steps of the synagogue in Capernaum, the same black basalt steps you once watched a crowd spill down. He pats the wall as he works. “A Roman paid for every stone of this,” he says. “Ask me how I feel about that.”
What do you ask an elder of the Capernaum synagogue?
Jesus went with them. When he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him, “Lord, don’t trouble yourself, for I am not worthy for you to come under my roof.

Therefore I didn’t even think myself worthy to come to you; but say the word, and my servant will be healed. For I also am a man placed under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go!’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come!’ and he comes; and to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
We said he was worthy. He said he was not. I have thought about that for a long time.
speaker: An elder of the Capernaum synagogue

text: He goes back to his sweeping. “A Roman, with more faith than the elders,” he says, without looking up. “He told us so to our faces. It was the kindest thing anyone ever said to me.”

After he had finished speaking in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum. A certain centurion’s servant, who was dear to him, was sick and at the point of death. When he heard about Jesus, he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him to come and save his servant.
When they came to Jesus, they begged him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy for you to do this for him, for he loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us.”
I begged a Jewish teacher to help a Roman officer. My grandfather would not have believed it. But that centurion loved this town, and the boy was dying.
speaker: An elder of the Capernaum synagogue

text: When Jesus heard these things, he marveled at him, and turned and said to the multitude who followed him, “I tell you, I have not found such great faith, no, not in Israel.” Those who were sent, returning to the house, found that the servant who had been sick was well.
“Not in Israel.” He said it with all of us standing there, the elders of Israel. And he was right.
speaker: An elder of the Capernaum synagogue
